title: Lists & Loops with *ngFor 🔁
description: Render arrays, access index, trackBy, and handle nested loops.

slides.title: Iterating Over Collections 🗂️
slides.content:
# *ngFor

`*ngFor` is a structural directive that repeats a template for each item in an iterable (array, Set, Map).

Syntax: `*ngFor="let item of items"`

* `let item` creates a template input variable that holds the current item.
* `items` is the iterable from the component.

It’s like a `for…of` loop embedded in your HTML.

slides.title: Simple To‑Do List

quizData.question: Which syntax correctly iterates over an array `items`?
quizData.explanation: The correct syntax is `let item of items`.

slides.title: Local Variables Inside *ngFor 📊
slides.content:
`*ngFor` provides several handy local variables:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `index` | number – the index of the current item (0‑based) |
| `first` | boolean – true if this is the first item |
| `last` | boolean – true if this is the last item |
| `even` | boolean – true if index is even |
| `odd` | boolean – true if index is odd |

These are exported by the directive; you assign them to a local variable: `let i = index`.

slides.title: trackBy: Performance Booster ⚡
slides.content:
By default, `*ngFor` tracks items by object identity. When the array is replaced (e.g., from an API), Angular destroys and recreates all DOM elements – expensive!

Use `trackBy` to tell Angular how to identify items uniquely:

1. Define a method in the component that returns a unique identifier.
2. Add `trackBy: myTrackFn` to the `*ngFor`.

Now Angular only re‑renders items that actually changed.

quizData.question: Using trackBy can improve performance when the iterable is replaced with a new array.
quizData.explanation: trackBy helps Angular identify which items have changed, added, or removed, avoiding unnecessary DOM recreation.

slides.title: Nested *ngFor Loops 🪆
slides.content:
You can nest `*ngFor` to render multi‑dimensional data: ```html

{{ category.name }}

  • {{ product.name }}
``` Be careful with performance on large data sets – try to flatten data if possible.
